key: old Hindi film song gets a remastered
name: ch00_song_remastered
alt: A sound engineer at a mixing desk cleans the hiss off an old film song: a crackly waveform from a vinyl record goes in, a clean waveform of the same shape comes out.
scene: A wide side view of a small recording studio in Mumbai, warm lamp light, soundproof foam panels on the back wall. On the LEFT, an old turntable on a wooden stand plays a worn black vinyl record with a faded label; from it a jagged, fuzzy waveform drawn as a ribbon full of little specks and spikes floats towards the centre, with tiny grey dots around it showing hiss. In the CENTRE, a sound engineer in his forties (grey kurta, rectangular spectacles, headphones round his neck) sits at a long mixing console with sliders and two knobs, one hand gently pushing a slider down, calm focused face. Above the console a small speech bubble holds a tick mark next to a microphone icon, showing the voice is kept as it is. On the RIGHT, the same waveform leaves the console and continues as a smooth, clean ribbon with exactly the same peaks and valleys, flowing into a shiny new record sleeve leaning on a shelf. A thin dashed outline under both waveforms shows the tune is the same shape before and after. Labels: "OLD" above the noisy waveform on the left, "REMASTERED" above the clean waveform on the right. Soft, warm, respectful mood, as if restoring an heirloom.

name: ch00_english_class_people_module
alt: A spoken-English teacher pins a new PEOPLE poster beside the GRAMMAR board while students practise a nervous mock interview and many hands go up for the new module.
scene: A classroom inside a small coaching centre in Chennai, ceiling fan turning, plastic chairs in rows, a whiteboard on the left wall. On the LEFT half, the whiteboard shows neat grammar notes drawn as simple lines and a tense table, with the label "GRAMMAR" written large at its top. Standing beside it, the teacher (woman in her thirties, green cotton sari, hair in a bun, marker in hand) is pinning a fresh bright poster to the wall next to the board; the poster shows two simple faces talking with a handshake between them and the label "PEOPLE". In the CENTRE foreground, a mock interview role play: a young man in a formal shirt sits stiffly in front of a student playing the manager, who raises a finger to interrupt; the young man's face is frozen, with a small grey zig-zag over his head showing panic. On the RIGHT, four students in a row lean forward eagerly, three of them with hands raised towards the new poster, one girl smiling. A small arrow from the poster to the raised hands shows where the interest went. Afternoon light through barred windows, encouraging mood.

key: the best batsman is not automatically
name: ch00_cricket_captain_armband
alt: In a cricket dressing room the best batsman quietly oils his bat while the player with the captain's armband calms a sulking fast bowler with a hand on his shoulder.
scene: A cricket team dressing room in an Indian stadium, wooden lockers and hooks with whites hanging on the back wall, a team list sheet pinned near the door. On the LEFT, the star batsman (mid twenties, white kit, pads still on) sits alone on a bench, absorbed in rubbing oil onto his bat, a small cluster of shining stars floating above the bat to show his skill; label "SKILL" floats above him. In the CENTRE and RIGHT, the captain (late twenties, white kit with a bright armband on his left sleeve, cap pushed back) stands beside the fast bowler, who slumps on a bench with crossed arms, towel over his neck and a scowling face. The captain rests one hand on the bowler's shoulder and gestures with the other as if explaining a plan; small curved lines from his mouth to the bowler show the talk. Behind them two other players look on, one nodding. A thin line from the captain to a phone on the bench hints at the call with the selectors. Label "CAPTAIN" above the captain and bowler pair. Warm late afternoon light from a high window, a calm, human mood: the skill earns the seat, the people work earns the armband.

key: A startup in Pune interviews every user
name: ch00_survey_society_gap
alt: Two young founders survey a whole housing society with clipboards; a big tally board shows fitness first and dealing with people second, and an empty shelf marks the missing product.
scene: A sunny courtyard of a mid-rise housing society in Pune, with a six-storey building of balconies, potted plants and clothes drying in the background. On the LEFT, two young founders (a woman in a yellow kurta with a lanyard, a man in a teal T-shirt and backpack) stand at a folding table with clipboards and long printed questionnaires, while a retired uncle in a cap and a young mother holding a toddler answer them. In the CENTRE, a large easel board shows a simple tally chart drawn with two thick bars: a tall amber bar labelled "FITNESS" and a shorter but still big teal bar labelled "PEOPLE", with three tiny face icons (a boss, an elder relative, a group) under the teal bar. On the RIGHT, a store shelf drawn as a wooden rack has a few thick books with no titles and a theory symbol on their spines, and one clearly empty slot outlined with a dashed line and a glowing light bulb above it, labelled "GAP". A dotted arrow runs from the teal bar to the empty slot. Bright morning light, curious and hopeful mood: the gap is the product.

key: A grandmother putting together the family
name: ch00_grandmother_recipe_sources
alt: A grandmother writes the family recipe book only after gathering from old cookbooks, a neighbour with a biryani pot, a cousin on the phone and a wedding caterer.
scene: A cosy home dining table in an Indian colony flat, evening, a steel tumbler of tea at her elbow. In the CENTRE, a grandmother in her seventies (cream cotton sari, round spectacles, white hair in a bun) sits writing in a thick handmade notebook labelled "RECIPE BOOK" on its cover, pen in hand, concentrating. Around her, four sources arranged in a loose circle, each with a dotted arrow pointing into the notebook: TOP LEFT, a stack of three old stained cookbooks with bookmarks; BOTTOM LEFT, the neighbour (a cheerful woman in a purple salwar) holding up a big biryani handi with steam rising; TOP RIGHT, a smartphone on speaker showing a cousin in a chef's white jacket, with a speech bubble; BOTTOM RIGHT, a wedding caterer in a cap stirring a giant cauldron on a gas burner. Inside the notebook, one small tick mark beside a line where the arrows converge, showing that only what appears in all sources is written down, while one stray idea from a single source floats off to the side with a small grey cross. A curious granddaughter peeks over the back of her chair, watching. Warm yellow lamp light, gentle family mood.

key: chutney recipe. Season one it is a few
name: ch00_chutney_recipe_grows
alt: A chutney vendor's recipe grows from a scrap of paper to a notebook to a thick family book as customers call out tastes like too sour and more garlic.
scene: An evening scene at a street-food cart in an Indian town, string lights and a steel chutney bucket on the cart. In the FOREGROUND CENTRE, the vendor (fifties, white vest, checked lungi, towel over shoulder) ladles green chutney onto a plate, listening. On the right of the cart, three regular customers hold paper plates: a college girl, an office man with a helmet under his arm, and an older auntie; two of them have small speech bubbles reading "too sour" and "more garlic", and arrows run from the bubbles to the vendor. Along the BOTTOM of the picture runs a left-to-right timeline of the recipe: first a small torn scrap of paper with three lines on it, labelled "YEAR 1"; then a slim spiral notebook with more lines and a few crossings-out; then a thick bound book with a ribbon, labelled "YEAR 15", with two family members (a son and a daughter) standing beside it each holding an identical bowl of chutney. A curved arrow loops from the customers back to the recipe line, showing the feedback loop. Warm evening light, lively market mood.

key: The wall of a coaching institute in Kota
name: ch00_kota_toppers_wall
alt: A student looks up at a coaching institute wall full of smiling topper photos while, just outside the frame, faded outlines of students who worked hard and did not get in stand unseen.
scene: A corridor of a coaching institute in Kota, tiled floor, a notice board and a water cooler. On the LEFT two thirds, a big wall is covered in a neat grid of framed photos of smiling students (simple generic faces, varied hair and clothes), each frame with a small ribbon; one large frame in the middle carries a banner reading "RANK 37". Across the top of the wall the label "TOPPERS" in bold. In the FOREGROUND, a teenage boy in a school bag and hoodie stands with his back half to us, looking up at the wall, impressed, his mother beside him holding a brochure. On the RIGHT third, beyond the edge of the wall and separated by a thin vertical line, a group of five students is drawn only as faded grey outlines with books under their arms, unlit, with a small question mark above them, labelled "UNSEEN". A faint dashed outline of an extra frame hangs beside them, empty. Bright tube light on the wall, dimmer light on the right side, a thoughtful mood: the wall shows some winners, not the whole count.

key: Most of us use a smartphone like a phone
name: ch00_phone_hidden_features
alt: A friend taps an ordinary smartphone and hidden features pop out of the screen (a document scanner, a live signboard translator, a bill payment) while the owner stares amazed.
scene: A bright living room in a Tamil Nadu home, afternoon. On the LEFT, the phone owner (a man in his fifties, checked half-sleeve shirt, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead) sits on a sofa with eyebrows raised and mouth open in surprise. Beside him, his niece (early twenties, teal kurta, ponytail) leans in and taps the screen of the large smartphone he is holding. In the CENTRE, drawn large, the phone screen glows, and three feature cards burst out of it on curved arrows like opening drawers: a sheet of paper with a scan frame around it; a road signboard with curly script turning into plain letters with a swap arrow; and an electricity bill with a lightning bolt and a green tick. On the RIGHT, a faint older-style phone sits on a side table with just three tiny icons (a call handset, a chat bubble and a camera), showing how he used it before. Label "HIDDEN" above the bursting feature cards, and "CALLS ONLY" under the old-style phone on the right. No brand logos anywhere. Warm daylight, delighted mood of discovering power that was always there.

key: Two people join the same gym in January
name: ch00_gym_two_reasons
alt: Split picture: a New Year joiner's treadmill sits empty in March, while a man with a borderline sugar report and a wedding invitation in mind runs at 6 a.m.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line, the same neighbourhood gym in both halves with the same treadmill, the same wall clock and the same trainer in a red T-shirt. LEFT panel: the wall calendar shows March, the clock reads nine in the evening; the treadmill stands empty with a towel hanging on it and a little cobweb in the corner of the handrail, and a faded thought bubble shows fireworks and the number of a new year. A small grey cross hangs beside the empty machine. Label "NEW YEAR" across the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the clock reads six in the morning and the window is still blue with dawn; a man in his early fifties (grey T-shirt with sweat patches, tracksuit trousers, determined face) runs hard on the treadmill. Above him a thought bubble holds two items: a lab report sheet with an arrow pointing up into an amber zone, and a red wedding invitation card with a small heart. The trainer stands beside him giving a thumbs up. A green tick floats near the runner. Label "REASON" across the top of the right panel. Clean morning light on the right, dim evening on the left.

name: ch00_highlights_vs_coach
alt: Split picture: a fan on a sofa enjoys a cricket highlights reel with a big six, while a coach at a desk pauses the same match on one delivery and sketches a field placement.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line, the same match on a screen in both halves. LEFT panel: a living room at night, a young man (twenties, jersey, shorts) lounges on a sofa with a bowl of snacks, cheering with one fist up as the television shows a batsman hitting a big six, with motion lines and a fast-forward symbol in the corner of the screen; small stars around the screen show the exciting moments flying by. Label "HIGHLIGHTS" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: a coach's office, a woman coach in her forties (team tracksuit, cap, spectacles) sits at a desk, one hand on a remote pointed at a laptop showing the same ground with the ball frozen mid-air and a large pause symbol. In front of her an open notebook shows a circle of a cricket field with small dots for fielders and an arrow moving one of them, and a question mark beside it. A small speech bubble over her head contains a question mark. Label "COACH" at the top of the right panel. Warm lamp light on the right, the glow of the TV on the left: same match, different learning.

key: Learning a multiplication table as a child
name: ch00_tables_morning_chant
alt: Children in a school classroom chant the seventeen times table in the morning, and in an inset a grown woman at an office desk rereads a contract, the same habit in adult form.
scene: A primary school classroom in India in the morning, sunlight slanting through tall windows, wooden benches. On the LEFT and CENTRE, a row of five children in school uniforms (white shirts, navy shorts and pinafores, oiled hair, one girl with two plaits) sit upright with mouths open in a chant, musical-note style curves rising from them. On the blackboard behind them, in chalk, a column of a times table with the last line "17 x 7 = 119" circled. A small sun icon and a calendar strip with many tick marks run along the top of the board, showing that the chant happens every morning. Label "EVERY DAY" above the calendar strip. On the RIGHT, an inset rounded panel with a thin border shows a grown woman office manager (forties, blue blouse, spectacles) at a desk with a lamp, turning the pages of a stapled contract with a pen in hand and a sticky note on it, with a small circular arrow showing she reads it again. Label "REVIEW" under the inset panel. A dotted line joins the chanting children to the inset. Fresh, cheerful morning light, a calm studious mood.

key: A first-aid card taped inside the kitchen
name: ch00_first_aid_card
alt: In a home kitchen a woman with a burnt hand reaches past butter and toothpaste to read a first-aid card taped inside the cupboard door, and the card shows a running tap for twenty minutes.
scene: A home kitchen in an Indian flat, steel utensils on a rack, a pressure cooker on the gas stove with a pan whose handle is still hot (small heat lines). In the CENTRE, a woman in her thirties (orange salwar kameez, dupatta tucked in) holds her reddened right hand away from her body, wincing. On the counter to the LEFT sit a butter dish and a toothpaste tube, each with a red cross over it, and a faint arrow of her first impulse curving towards them, then bending away. On the RIGHT, the cupboard door above the counter is open and a white card is taped inside with four strips of tape; the card shows a simple tap with water drops, a hand under it and a small clock face, with the short text "20 MIN". A green tick sits beside the card. Below the cupboard, the kitchen tap runs with blue water lines, ready. Label "CHECK FIRST" above the open cupboard door. A teenage son peeks in from the doorway on the far left, concerned. Bright daylight from a small window, a calm, practical mood: the habit is to look before acting on instinct.

key: every time someone swears, a coin goes in
name: ch00_hostel_swear_jar
alt: In a college hostel room a student sheepishly drops a coin into a swear jar while his roommates laugh, and an inset shows the month-end plate of samosas the jar buys.
scene: A cramped college hostel room in India, two bunk beds with bedsheets, a study table with books and a table fan, posters on the wall without any text. In the CENTRE on the table, a big clear glass jar half full of coins with a paper label reading "SWEAR JAR". A student (nineteen, grey hoodie, messy hair) leans over and drops a coin into it, with a guilty grin and one hand on the back of his neck; a little coin-fall motion line shows the coin dropping. On the LEFT, a roommate sitting on the lower bunk points at him and laughs; on the RIGHT, another roommate holding a laptop grins and gives a thumbs up, and a third on the top bunk peeks over the edge. On the wall above the jar, a calendar shows the month with a circle around the last day. In the TOP RIGHT corner, an inset round bubble shows the month-end treat: a steel plate piled with golden samosas and four hands reaching in. Label "MONTH END" under the inset bubble. Warm evening tube light, friendly, teasing mood: nobody resents the jar, and everyone notices their habit.

key: A shopkeeper in an old Indian market
name: ch00_bahi_khata_saturday
alt: Late on a Saturday night a shopkeeper in an old market shop goes through his red bahi-khata ledger line by line under a hanging bulb, ticking and crossing entries.
scene: A narrow old cloth shop in an Indian market at night, shutter half down at the front, folded bolts of fabric stacked on wooden shelves behind. A single bulb hangs from a wire, throwing a warm circle of light. In the CENTRE, the shopkeeper (sixties, white kurta, Gandhi-style white cap, thick spectacles on his nose) sits cross-legged on a white mattress behind a low wooden desk, running one finger down the page of a big red cloth-bound ledger tied with a string. On the open page, lines of entries with small green ticks beside some and red crosses beside others, and one line circled with a frown face drawn next to it to mark a lost customer. On the wall to the LEFT, a calendar with the day "SAT" circled. To the RIGHT, on a shelf, a long row of older red ledgers, one for every year, their spines lined up to show many years of the same habit. A small clock on the wall reads ten. Label "WEEKLY AUDIT" across the top. Quiet, honest, slightly tired mood, warm light against the dark market: some totals make him wince, but he reads every line.

key: A new parent's notebook of a baby
name: ch00_baby_firsts_notebook
alt: A tired new father at night writes in a notebook of his baby's firsts (smile, word, steps, each with a date) while the baby sleeps in a cradle beside him.
scene: A small bedroom in an Indian flat at night, a night lamp glowing, a ceiling fan above. On the RIGHT, a wooden cradle hung from a frame, the baby asleep under a light blanket with a tiny fist by its face. On the LEFT, a new father in his early thirties (crumpled T-shirt, pyjamas, dark circles under his eyes, a small smile) sits on the edge of the bed with a hardcover notebook open on his knee, pen in hand. The notebook is drawn large and slightly tilted towards the viewer: three entries in a column, each with a tiny icon and a short date, a smiling face icon, a speech bubble icon and a little footprint icon. A small rising staircase line along the edge of the page shows progress. Above the notebook a soft glow and the label "FIRSTS". Beside him on the bedside table, a mug of milk and a baby bottle. A dotted line runs from the cradle to the notebook, connecting each moment to its line in the book. Calm, tender, slightly sleepy mood, warm amber night light: on a tired night the record shows that things are moving forward.
